newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply off as base metals slide.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply off as base metals slide.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply lower, dragged down by the slide in base and precious metals, but further sharp losses were ruled out for the time being, traders said.
Copper's boost from Tuesday's news of production difficulties at Southern Peru Copper due to flooding wore off overnight as it became factored into the price, traders added.
COMEX opened weaker and continued to drift lower for much of the session.
"There is still a very tight inventory situation and that should prevent a major downtrend," David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said.
"But I think the market will have problems in reaching the recent highs unless there is some improved demand at the higher price levels," Rinehimer added.
May COMEX settled 2.60 cents weaker at 110.40 cents a lb, traded 113.20 to 110.00 cents. Spot March went out 2.05 cents off at 113.65 cents.
Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots compared to Tuesday's official 6,848 lots.
The market was closely watching developments at SPCC. A spokesman for ASARCO, which controls SPCC, said on Wednesday there were no further details available.

Chile's Quebrada Blanca mine said its February copper output was lower than expected because heavy rainfall in the northern Atacama desert damaged access roads and slowed the pit's heap leaching process.
Quebrada Blanca produced 4,633 tonnes of cathode in February, down from planned output of 6,000 tonnes.
